description:
From docs/research/sat-solver.md (defk-dtw.21): Ash-sized formulas (~27 variables, 63 clauses) solve in 4-82 us in picosat_elixir, about what packing the CNF into binaries costs (~31 us measured), so a kernel used as a per-call drop-in for simple_sat/picosat lands marginal at best. A short guidance entry once the CDCL kernel exists (sibling ticket under defk-52v): the same kernel called per formula vs batched over Crux's enumeration, with the crossover by formula size reported in the sweep. Expected: marginal or poor per call; the batch form is the catalog entry that helps.

Blocked by the CDCL kernel ticket. Done when: the per-call example runs in run_all.exs with its pre-registered verdict and the README row says "batch it".

comments.text: Landed on branch defk-9p6.25/sat-per-call-guidance. examples/cdcl_sat_per_call.exs (loads cdcl_sat.exs's kernel via DEFK_SAT_LIB=1, no second compile; cdcl_sat.exs wraps its checks/reports in unless DEFK_SAT_LIB), README row, docs/performance.md 5.11. PRE-REGISTERED marginal/poor per call; MEASURED (M4 Pro, load 3-8, four runs, provisional, baseline optimised): per call under Crux vs best Elixir solver: 5-11 vars 0.6-0.9x poor (tiny line 0.67-0.82x), 16 vars 1.1-1.6x marginal, 26-28 vars 2.4-2.8x GOOD (Ash-sized line 2.5-2.8x, Elixir 16.5-17.4 vs defk 6.3-6.5 ms), 37-50 3.8-5.1x, 109-166 4.3-5.0x. Crossover to 2x between 16 and 26 vars. vs picosat per call: 1.3-1.75x faster at 5-26 vars (single solve), 2.5-3.9x at 50-166; 1.1-1.8x inside Crux. Batched vs per-call kernel, same enumeration: 1.9-3.8x from 16 to 166 vars (1.4-3.4 us/solve vs 2.5-9.4; 11.7-19.8 vs 29-45 at 109-166); one-solve formulas batch loses 0.7-0.8x. Call boundary 0.4-0.7 us; per-call cost is Elixir-side list building + packing (the research's 31 us packing figure does not hold). Guidance: per call fine from ~20 vars, stay Elixir below ~12, batch whenever one question makes several solves. Deviation: README says 'batch it' conditionally, not 'per call is a trap', because the numbers say per call is good at Ash size; DEFK_RESULT expected is :good for the Ash line (precedent cdcl_sat_s1/per_pair_distance) so run_all does not fail, the pre-registered text is in the header; the tiny line registers :poor. run_all full run not executed (cdcl_sat.exs ~minutes); both scripts run standalone, format, docs tests, mix docs pass.

title: Guidance example: a per-call SAT drop-in for simple_sat repeats the tiny-calls trap
